text: i18n: select shipping languages and write the translations

Language set DECIDED by the user: en, de, es, fr, pt-BR, zh-Hans, ja, ar, uk (nine). Arabic ships in the first wave rather than being deferred, so RTL is in scope from the start — split out as its own ticket. Storage of the user's choice is device-local, not account-synced, so there is no server or wire-contract work anywhere in this epic. Ukrainian costs nothing extra on the plural axis now that T-123 removed plural handling from the codebase entirely — worth noting, since Ukrainian otherwise needs 3-4 forms. Remaining open question for this ticket: ar and uk translations need a native reviewer; the domain terms called out in the body (backlog as a status, step-up password, shopping-list vs checklist) are the ones machine translation gets wrong.

CONTENT COMPLETE, DELIBERATELY LEFT OPEN. 2799 strings: 9 languages x (135 web keys + 198 android strings), landed across bf19d8f / 88489f1 / deda85c / 28c4467. verify-all PASS on all three stages.

WHY THIS IS STILL OPEN: the mechanical properties are guaranteed by tests that run on every build (key parity, format-arg parity, stray-script, non-empty — see web i18n.test.ts and android TranslationResourcesTest). The linguistic quality is guaranteed by nothing. For six of the nine languages nobody working on this repo can read the output, so 'it looked right' was never an available check. Closing this would record a confidence that does not exist.

NEEDS NATIVE REVIEW, in priority order:

1. 'backlog' — the one term that varies deliberately by language: Backlog (de), Mas tarde / Plus tard / Mais tarde (es/fr/pt), 稍后 / あとで (zh/ja), Пізніше (uk), قائمة الانتظار (ar). Each is natural standing alone; whether that inconsistency is acceptable across one product is a judgement I made and cannot validate. The status_backlog_hint string carries the precise definition in every language, which is what makes the variance survivable.

2. Register — informal throughout (tu/tu/voce/ти/Du), EXCEPT Japanese, which uses です・ます because plain form reads brusque in a Japanese UI. If that choice is wrong for a language it is wrong in every single one of its strings, so it is worth checking before anything else linguistic.

3. German — the user will review at the next release. Du-form, and Backlog kept as a loanword rather than Merkliste/Vorrat.

ALSO WORTH KNOWING: one real corruption was caught during this work — Cyrillic spliced into a Japanese string ('直接открытьいて'). It was found by re-reading, not by process, which is why the stray-script check now exists on both clients. Assume that class of error is the one most likely to have survived elsewhere.
